I couldn't finish writing `chunk_00.json`. Running the build script needs your approval, and this session can't prompt for it, so the file still holds only `[]`.

All 17 searches ran. The script that assembles them into the required JSON is written, but I never ran it. It is at `dataset_builder/results_sample/_build_chunk00.py`. I did not delete it, so run it yourself with `python -I _build_chunk00.py` from that folder. Then delete the script.

What the script will write:
- **Entries:** 17, all with `results` populated: 5 for `2hop__67660_81007`, 5 for `sample_2hop_b` and 7 for `sample_3hop_c`.
- **Snippets:** Many results will have an empty `snippet` with a `fetch_error`. Fetches returned 403, 404 or 405 for several pages, one page gave a bot-check, and some top-3 results were mirror or scraper domains that I skipped.
- **Snippet length:** The fetched snippets are short, mostly one or two sentences under about 125 characters. The fetch tool capped quotes from non-whitelisted sites at that length, so the 300–500 character target was not reachable.
- **WebFetch:** I don't have WebFetch in this session, so I fetched through the `web-fetch` subagent. For each search, 3 to 9 distinct fetches were shared across the searches that returned the same URL. The script reuses one snippet per URL across every search where that URL appears.
- **Rank and low-value domains:** I mark results beyond rank 3 `beyond_top3_not_fetched`. Low-value domains such as IPFS gateways and scraper clones get `skipped_low_value_domain` at any rank.
- **Timestamp:** All 17 entries carry the same timestamp, taken when the script runs, because I couldn't write each entry as its search finished.
